meta.name: Create SQLAlchemy declarative base and session factory

context.prd-excerpt:
Link Shelf is a local, single-user link store. From the PRD overview: "One endpoint to save a link, one to get them all back, and tags so the list stays navigable past a few dozen entries." No authentication, no multi-tenancy, no sharing.
From the PRD's tech-stack rationale, which is the direct reason this task exists and why it is shaped the way it is:
"SQLite rather than PostgreSQL so the whole project runs with no external service: a fixture that needs a database server running is a fixture that fails for reasons unrelated to what is being tested."
Three models will be defined on the base this task creates - Link (L4-002), Tag and LinkTag (L4-003) - and three endpoints will take a session from the get_db dependency this task creates (L3-003, L3-004, L3-006).
context.tech-stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI 0.110+, SQLAlchemy 2.x (declarative style: DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column), SQLite (file-backed, no server process), pytest 8.x, httpx. Backend only - no frontend, no container runtime.

task.objective: Create app/db.py: the SQLAlchemy 2.x declarative Base that every model in this project subclasses, a file-backed SQLite engine with foreign-key enforcement switched on, a session factory, an explicit init_db() that creates the schema with Base.metadata.create_all, and the get_db FastAPI dependency that yields a session and closes it afterwards.

requirements.requirement: Create file `app/db.py`. It must define exactly these six module-level names, all of which later tasks import by name: `DATABASE_PATH`, `DATABASE_URL`, `engine`, `SessionLocal`, `Base`, `init_db`, `get_db`.

Define the database location relative to the file, not to the process working directory, so that the path is the same whether pytest is invoked from the repository root or elsewhere:
from pathlib import Path
DATABASE_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "link_shelf.db" DATABASE_URL = f"sqlite:///{DATABASE_PATH}"
`parent.parent` resolves to the repository root because this file is app/db.py. The file name is exactly `link_shelf.db`. .gitignore already ignores `*.db` and `*.db-journal` (created by L0-001), so this generated file is never committed.

Create the engine:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
`check_same_thread=False` is required because FastAPI serves requests on a threadpool while a session created on one thread may be used on another. Do not pass `echo=True`; nothing in the PRD asks for SQL logging and it makes the test output unreadable.

Switch on SQLite foreign-key enforcement for every connection. SQLite ignores FOREIGN KEY clauses unless the pragma is set per connection, which would make LinkTag's foreign keys to links.id and tags.id (L4-003) decorative:
from sqlalchemy import event from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
@event.listens_for(Engine, "connect") def _set_sqlite_pragma(dbapi_connection, connection_record): cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor() cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON") cursor.close()
Register the listener on the `Engine` CLASS, not on the `engine` instance. This is deliberate: it means the throwaway engine that L4-004's db_session fixture creates per test also enforces foreign keys, without L4-004 having to duplicate this listener. SQLite is the only dialect in this project, so a class-wide listener issuing a PRAGMA is safe here.
Use a cursor. `dbapi_connection.execute(...)` is not available on a raw sqlite3 Connection in the way this listener needs; `cursor.execute(...)` followed by `cursor.close()` is the documented SQLAlchemy recipe.

Create the session factory:
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
SessionLocal = sessionmaker( bind=engine, autoflush=False, autocommit=False, expire_on_commit=False, )
`expire_on_commit=False` is required, not optional: POST /links (L3-003) commits a Link and then returns its attributes in the response body. With the SQLAlchemy default of True, every attribute would be expired at commit and reading `link.id` would emit a second SELECT against a session the request is about to close.

Define the declarative base:
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase
class Base(DeclarativeBase): """Declarative base for every Link Shelf model."""
Use `DeclarativeBase` (SQLAlchemy 2.x). Do NOT use `declarative_base()`, the 1.4-era factory function: the project declares SQLAlchemy 2.x and L4-002 and L4-003 are written against the `Mapped` / `mapped_column` annotation style, which requires this base.

Define schema creation as an explicit function, never as an import-time side effect:
def init_db() -> None: """Create every table registered on Base.metadata.""" import app.models # noqa: F401 - importing registers the models on Base.metadata
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
The `import app.models` must be INSIDE the function body. At module level it would be a circular import: app/models/link.py imports Base from this module.
The import is what makes create_all useful. `Base.metadata.create_all` only creates tables for model classes that have actually been imported; without this line the call would create nothing at all once models exist.
Do NOT call `init_db()` at module level. Importing app.db must not create a file on disk.

Define the FastAPI dependency:
from collections.abc import Generator from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
def get_db() -> Generator[Session, None, None]: """Yield a SQLAlchemy session. Closes on request completion.""" db = SessionLocal() try: yield db finally: db.close()
The `finally` is required: without it a handler that raises leaks the connection back to nothing and the pool is exhausted after enough failed requests.
Note on the annotation: L3-004's dependency block writes this signature as `from typing import Generator`. `collections.abc.Generator` is the correct spelling for Python 3.11 and is the same type at runtime, so the contract is unchanged. Use `collections.abc`; the difference is recorded here rather than left as a silent divergence.
Do NOT commit or roll back inside get_db. Whether a unit of work commits is the handler's decision, and a dependency that committed on the way out would make L3-003's "store nothing" requirement impossible to honour.

Do NOT create a migrations directory, an alembic.ini, or a versioned migration chain, and do not add alembic to pyproject.toml. Neither the PRD's declared stack nor L0-003's dependency list contains a migration tool. Schema creation in this project is `Base.metadata.create_all` and nothing else.
Do NOT define any model class in this file, and do not modify app/models/__init__.py. Link is L4-002's; Tag and LinkTag are L4-003's.

task.test-requirements:
Test policy: TDD, runner pytest. Write tests/test_db.py FIRST, watch it fail on the missing `app.db` module, then create app/db.py until it passes.
Create test file: `tests/test_db.py`.
This file must NOT use a `db_session` or `client` fixture. tests/conftest.py is created by L4-004, which depends on this task; depending on it here would be circular. Build whatever each test needs from `app.db` directly.
import pytest from sqlalchemy import inspect, text from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Session
from app.db import DATABASE_PATH, DATABASE_URL, Base, SessionLocal, engine, get_db, init_db
This test cites no acceptance criterion. No criterion in this PRD describes the declarative base, the engine or the session factory - see the note on <source-feature>.
Test: test_base_is_a_sqlalchemy_2_declarative_base - Assert `issubclass(Base, DeclarativeBase)` is True - Assert `Base is not DeclarativeBase` (a subclass was defined, not re-exported) - Assert `hasattr(Base, "metadata")` is True - Asserts requirement 6. Cites no acceptance criterion.
Test: test_engine_is_file_backed_sqlite_at_the_repository_root - Assert `engine.url.get_backend_name() == "sqlite"` - Assert `DATABASE_PATH.name == "link_shelf.db"` - Assert `DATABASE_PATH.parent == pathlib.Path("app").resolve().parent`, proving the path is the repository root and is derived from the module location rather than the working directory - Assert `DATABASE_URL == f"sqlite:///{DATABASE_PATH}"` - Asserts requirements 2 and 3. Cites no acceptance criterion.
Test: test_foreign_key_enforcement_is_on_for_every_connection - Build a throwaway engine on a temp path: `probe = create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'probe.db'}")` (pytest's `tmp_path`) - `with probe.connect() as conn: value = conn.execute(text("PRAGMA foreign_keys")).scalar()` - Assert `value == 1` - This proves requirement 4 registered the listener on the Engine CLASS rather than on the single module-level `engine` instance: a listener bound only to `engine` would leave this independently-created engine at SQLite's default of 0, and L4-004's per-test engine would silently not enforce LinkTag's foreign keys. - Also assert `probe.dispose()` runs without error, then `probe.dispose()` - Cites no acceptance criterion.
Test: test_session_factory_is_configured_for_the_request_lifecycle - `session = SessionLocal()` - Assert `isinstance(session, Session)` - Assert `session.get_bind() is engine` - Assert `session.autoflush is False` - Assert `session.expire_on_commit is False`, the setting L3-003 depends on to read `link.id` after commit - `session.close()` - Asserts requirement 5. Cites no acceptance criterion.
Test: test_get_db_yields_a_session_and_closes_it - `generator = get_db()` - `session = next(generator)` - Assert `isinstance(session, Session)` - `session.execute(text("SELECT 1"))` - Assert `session.get_transaction() is not None` - executing began a transaction - `with pytest.raises(StopIteration): next(generator)` - exhausting the generator runs the `finally` block - Assert `session.get_transaction() is None` - close() released the transaction, proving the `finally: db.close()` of requirement 8 actually ran - Cites no acceptance criterion.
Test: test_get_db_closes_the_session_even_when_the_caller_raises - `generator = get_db()` - `session = next(generator)` - `session.execute(text("SELECT 1"))` - `with pytest.raises(RuntimeError): generator.throw(RuntimeError("handler blew up"))` - Assert `session.get_transaction() is None` - This is the reason requirement 8 uses try/finally rather than closing after the yield: a handler that raises must still return its connection to the pool. - Cites no acceptance criterion.
Test: test_importing_app_db_creates_no_file - Assert `"init_db" in dir(__import__("app.db", fromlist=["init_db"]))` - Assert `callable(init_db)` - Assert that `app/db.py`, read as text with `pathlib.Path("app/db.py").read_text()`, contains no line that is exactly `init_db()` at column 0 - i.e. `init_db()` is defined but never invoked at module level (requirement 7) - Concretely: `assert not any(line.strip() == "init_db()" for line in pathlib.Path("app/db.py").read_text().splitlines())` - Cites no acceptance criterion.
Test: test_init_db_creates_the_database_and_is_idempotent - `init_db()` - Assert `DATABASE_PATH.exists()` is True - Assert `isinstance(inspect(engine).get_table_names(), list)` - Do NOT assert an exact table list. At the point THIS task runs app/models/__init__.py is still empty, so the correct result is zero tables; after L4-002 and L4-003 the same call returns `["link_tags", "links", "tags"]`. Asserting `== []` here would turn L4-002 into a task that breaks a passing test in a file it does not own. The assertion above is written so that it stays true in both states. - `init_db()` a second time - assert it raises no exception, proving create_all is safe to call repeatedly (create_all passes checkfirst=True by default) - Asserts requirement 7. Cites no acceptance criterion.
Test: test_no_migration_tool_was_introduced - Assert `not pathlib.Path("migrations").exists()` - Assert `not pathlib.Path("alembic.ini").exists()` - Assert `"alembic" not in pathlib.Path("pyproject.toml").read_text()` - Asserts requirement 9. Cites no acceptance criterion.

Run: `python -c "from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase; from app.db import Base; assert issubclass(Base, DeclarativeBase) and Base is not DeclarativeBase; print('Base OK')"` - must print `Base OK`

Run: `python -c "from app.db import engine, DATABASE_PATH; assert engine.url.get_backend_name() == 'sqlite'; assert DATABASE_PATH.name == 'link_shelf.db'; print(DATABASE_PATH)"` - must print a path ending in `link_shelf.db`

Run: `python -c "from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text; from sqlalchemy.orm import Session; import app.db; e = create_engine('sqlite://'); c = e.connect(); assert c.execute(text('PRAGMA foreign_keys')).scalar() == 1; print('foreign keys enforced')"` - must print `foreign keys enforced`, proving the pragma listener is registered on the Engine class

Run: `python -c "import pathlib; src = pathlib.Path('app/db.py').read_text(); assert not any(l.strip() == 'init_db()' for l in src.splitlines()); assert 'declarative_base(' not in src; assert 'alembic' not in src; print('module-level cleanliness OK')"` - must print `module-level cleanliness OK`
Run: `pytest tests/test_db.py -v` - all 9 test functions pass
Run: `pytest tests/ -v` - the whole suite passes, proving app/db.py did not break the layer-3 tests already merged into this worktree

# app/db.py from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase
class Base(DeclarativeBase): """Declarative base for every Link Shelf model."""
# Every model in this project subclasses this and nothing else: # app/models/link.py class Link(Base) __tablename__ = "links" (L4-002) # app/models/tag.py class Tag(Base) __tablename__ = "tags" (L4-003) # app/models/link_tag.py class LinkTag(Base) __tablename__ = "link_tags" (L4-003) # # A model is registered on Base.metadata only once its module has been imported. That is # what app/models/__init__.py is for.

# app/db.py from pathlib import Path from sqlalchemy import create_engine
DATABASE_PATH: Path # <repository root>/link_shelf.db (gitignored via *.db) DATABASE_URL: str # f"sqlite:///{DATABASE_PATH}"
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
# Foreign-key enforcement is switched on by an @event.listens_for(Engine, "connect") # listener registered in this module. It is bound to the Engine CLASS, so ANY engine # created anywhere in this process after app.db is imported also enforces foreign keys. # # FOR L4-004: this is why the db_session fixture does NOT need to register its own pragma # listener. Importing app.db (which the fixture does anyway, for Base and get_db) is # sufficient for the per-test engine to enforce LinkTag's FKs to links.id and tags.id.

# app/db.py from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
SessionLocal = sessionmaker( bind=engine, autoflush=False, autocommit=False, expire_on_commit=False, )
# expire_on_commit=False is a load-bearing setting, not a preference: handlers read model # attributes AFTER commit to build their response. L4-004's per-test sessionmaker must be # configured identically or L3-003's POST /links tests will pass in production and fail # under test for reasons unrelated to the handler.

# app/db.py def init_db() -> None: """Create every table registered on Base.metadata.""" import app.models # noqa: F401 Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

It is not applied here because doing so would # reopen a file this task does not own and would contradict L3-002's requirement 3.
